Despite Mac shipments falling 11% in Q3 2026, Apple's market share rose from 8.5% to 9.5% as the overall market shipments dropped significantly by 20.1%, according to IDC's latest report. Details below.

Apple outperforms most of the PC market in a challenging environment

IDC today released its Q3 2026 global PC shipment report, noting that although Mac shipments were down compared to the same period last year, Apple clearly outperformed the overall market.

According to IDC preliminary data, Apple shipped a total of 5.9 million Macs in Q3 2026, a decrease of 11.3% from 6.7 million in the same period last year.

However, the overall PC market saw an even more significant decline, with global shipments falling 20.1% year-over-year to 62.7 million units.

As a result, Apple's share of global PC shipments actually rose from 8.5% to 9.5%.

Apple remained in fourth place, behind Lenovo, HP, and Dell. Lenovo led with 14.9 million shipments and a 23.8% market share, followed by HP with 10.3 million shipments and a 16.5% share, while Dell had 7.6 million shipments and a 12.1% share.

Among the top five vendors, HP recorded the largest year-over-year decline, with shipments falling 30.9%. As for ASUS, shipments fell only 8.6% year-over-year, the smallest decline among the group, reaching 5.5 million units with an 8.7% market share.

Looking ahead, IDC noted that "channel concerns over high inventory and weak demand at high prices could lead to promotional incentives in the near term," and stated that "prices will remain at levels well above those of a year ago."

The firm also pointed out that economic conditions have weakened since the previous quarter, which may further dampen demand and "cast a further shadow over the remainder of 2026 and the outlook for 2027."
